description: Federal law already lets Georgia stay on standard time all year, without Congress. Why it would be the better choice for children’s safety.
shortAnswer: Federal law already lets a state stay on standard time all year. Georgia could do it on its own, without asking Congress. It means one less hour of darkness every winter school morning than permanent daylight saving time would bring.

sections.heading: The choice no one in Georgia is talking about
sections.shortAnswer: Under 15 U.S.C. § 260a, a state that lies entirely within one time zone may by law exempt itself from daylight saving time, as long as the whole state observes standard time. Georgia lies entirely within the Eastern time zone.

sections.heading: What standard time all year would mean for a Georgia school morning
sections.shortAnswer: On standard time, the sun comes up in Atlanta at about 7:43 on the darkest January mornings. Under permanent daylight saving time, it would be about 8:43.

sections.heading: We tried permanent daylight saving time once
sections.shortAnswer: In January 1974, during the energy crisis, the country went on daylight saving time all year. The country tried it, parents saw their children walking to school in the dark, and the country quit within the year.

sections.heading: The spring change itself is dangerous
sections.shortAnswer: Fatal crashes rose about 6 percent in the workweek after the spring change, about 28 more deaths a year. Standard time all year ends that change for good.

sections.heading: The honest objection: darker evenings
sections.shortAnswer: Some studies have found that moving daylight into the evening reduces pedestrian deaths. The school morning is not optional. A child has to be at the bus stop at the time the school district sets.

sections.heading: Is this pie in the sky?
sections.shortAnswer: This is the rare child safety problem that Georgia can fix by itself, with one law, at no cost.

faq.q: Can Georgia stay on standard time all year without Congress?
faq.a: Federal law already lets a state stay on standard time all year. Georgia lies entirely within the Eastern time zone. The General Assembly could pass that law in January. No one in Washington has to approve it.

faq.q: Is permanent standard time safer for children than permanent daylight saving time?
faq.a: It means one less hour of darkness every winter school morning than permanent daylight saving time would bring. A fatal crash involving a school-aged pedestrian was roughly twice as likely on dark mornings as after sunrise.

faq.q: What happened when the U.S. tried permanent daylight saving time in 1974?
faq.a: The New York Times reported that eight Florida schoolchildren were killed in accidents in the weeks after the change. Congress repealed it that October. A Department of Transportation study could not blame the increase on daylight saving time alone.

faq.q: Wouldn't permanent standard time make evenings more dangerous?
faq.a: Evening light matters too. Some studies have found that moving daylight into the evening reduces pedestrian deaths. But a family can often decide when practice ends, when the walk home happens, and whether someone drives.
